points.t: A **painless crusted nodule or ulcer with a rolled edge** on exposed skin, not healing after weeks of antibiotics, after travel or migration.
*Leishmania* parasites injected by **sandfly bites**, multiplying in dermal macrophages.
Refer to **tropical medicine** for biopsy / PCR and species-guided treatment; many Old World lesions heal on their own.
**Mucosal leishmaniasis** (New World species) and visceral disease in the immunosuppressed.

cause.lead: A protozoan living in skin macrophages.
points: Female **phlebotomine sandflies** (1.5–3 mm, silent) bite at **dusk and dawn**; bites go unnoticed.
Endemic: Latin America, **Mediterranean** (incl. southern Europe), Middle East, Central / South Asia, East Africa.
**Mucocutaneous** only with New World *Viannia* (*L. braziliensis*…): ~5% lifetime risk; months–years later.
Host immunity sets the form: localised, diffuse (anergic) or mucosal.

visuals.caption: A sandfly injects Leishmania into the dermis; parasite-laden macrophages form a granuloma that breaks down into a crusted ‘volcano’ ulcer with an indurated, violaceous rim.
visuals.alt: Skin cross-section with crusted crater ulcer and parasitised macrophages

features.lead: Slow, painless, exposed skin, weeks after travel.
points: Incubation **2 weeks–6 months** or more: ask about travel well before onset.
**Painless red papule** → nodule / plaque (1–5 cm) → **‘volcano’ ulcer** with **raised, rolled, indurated (violaceous) border** and crust.
Exposed sites: face, ears, forearms, hands, lower legs; single or several.
**Sporotrichoid** nodules along lymphatics, regional nodes (esp. *Viannia*). Heals with a scar.
Travel / residence + chronic painless non-healing ulcer on exposed skin.
From the **active raised edge**: unfixed in saline for **PCR** (species), formalin for histology.
ENT / nasal examination for mucosal disease.

cards.name: Infected insect bite
cards.clue: Acute, itchy / painful, resolves; no rolled edge.

cards.name: BCC / SCC
cards.clue: Older, sun-exposed, pearly or keratotic edge.

cards.name: Atypical mycobacteria
cards.clue: Fish tank (*M. marinum*), Buruli: undermined ulcer.

manage.lead: Recognise and refer. Don’t start empirical treatment.

points: Every suspected CL → **ID / tropical medicine** (e.g. HTD Leishmaniasis MDT, UCLH).
**Priority**: New World exposure, facial / joint / genital, > 4 cm or multiple, lymphatic spread, immunosuppression, mucosal symptoms.
Treat **clear secondary infection** per NICE (antibiotics won’t cure CL).
**Avoid potent topical steroids** on an undiagnosed ulcer.
Species-guided: local or systemic therapy; New World *Viannia* needs systemic treatment.

limits.t: Avoid dusk / dawn outdoors; long sleeves; DEET; permethrin clothing; **fine-mesh nets**; fans / AC; sleep off the ground.

visuals.caption: Sandflies are small enough to pass through standard mosquito nets (left); fine-mesh nets (right) keep them out.
visuals.alt: Coarse net with sandfly passing through beside a fine-mesh net

items.t: Mucosal destruction, fever, weight loss or splenomegaly (possible visceral disease), immunosuppression.
Nasal stuffiness, bleeding or oral / nasal ulcers months–years after New World CL: **mucosal leishmaniasis**.
Any suspected CL: tropical medicine referral.

pearls.t: A **‘non-healing insect bite’ > 4–6 weeks after travel** → ask about leishmaniasis.
Mediterranean holidays and Belize / Central America are common UK sources.
A healed skin lesion doesn’t exclude New World mucosal disease: report nose / mouth symptoms for years.
Not contagious; scarring is common: discuss facial-scar impact.

quiz.a: Painless ‘volcano’ ulcer with a raised rolled indurated border.

quiz.q: Where to biopsy and why send unfixed tissue?
quiz.a: Active edge; PCR identifies the species, which guides treatment.
